newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Film planned on U.S. student killed in S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Film planned on U.S. student killed in S.Africa.

text.p: A South African film producer said on Thursday he had begun work on a movie about Amy Biehl, the U.S. student who came to the country to do good but was murdered by a mob in a black township.

"The story of this young American woman needs to be told as she is a role model for people everywhere," said Anant Singh, whose previous productions include "Sarafina!" and "Cry, the Beloved Country".
Singh said he had obtained rights to the Amy Biehl story from the student's parents, Peter and Linda Biehl, two years ago. Work has begun on the script and filming is due to begin next year.
Amy Biehl was killed in August 1993 at the age of 26 when she drove into Guguletu township outside Cape Town to drop off three black friends.
The car was stopped and stoned by a crowd returning from a political rally. Members of the crowd chased Biehl and stabbed and stoned her to death.

Four youths convicted of her murder applied this week to Archbishop Desmond Tutu's Truth and Reconciliation Commission for amnesty. They said they killed Biehl because she was white and whites had stolen the country from blacks.
The commission is now assessing whether the crime was political, which would pave the way for the killers to be freed from 18-year jail terms.
Biehl's parents travelled to South Africa to attend the amnesty hearing. They said they would not oppose freedom for their daughter's murderers.
